newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent crude ends weaker but $22 support holds.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent crude ends weaker but $22 support holds.

text.p: IPE Brent crude futures ended weaker but off lows as long-term technical support held and a recovery in U.S. heating oil prices worked through to London, dealers said.
March Brent closed at $22.05 a barrel, down 21 cents but above the low of $22.00 seen as a key support level which was tested in early afternoon dealing.
Prompt Brent crude futures last traded below $22.00 a barrel over four months ago on September 23.
"We came down, tested support at $22.00 and then bounced back," said a broker.
"U.S. products have been leading the market and after starting weak from Friday they came back up, pulling the rest of the market with it," she added.
Brokers said selling interest was light ahead of Tuesday's industry inventory data and while temperatures remained cold.

Private forecaster Weather Services Corp said below normal temperatures in the U.S. Northeast, a key heating oil market, would moderate slightly on Tuesday "before becoming much colder again Wednesday and Thursday".
NYMEX heating oil futures added 0.53 cents a gallon to close at 67.30 cents after earlier touching a low of 65.30.
Earlier, IPE Feb gas oil also drew strength from gains in U.S. heating oil, closing just 25 cents down at $199.75 a tonne after posting a session low of $195.50.
